standard \u003ccode\u003ejson.dumps()\u003c/code\u003e, which immediately crashes if the state contains PyTorch tensors or multidimensional NumPy arrays. The \u003ccode\u003eTensorSafeEncoder\u003c/code\u003e intercepts these structures natively during the graph's execution and audit-logging phases.\nInstead of crashing or attempting to write gigabytes of floating-point values, it translates the mathematical states into safe, auditable metadata (e.g. \u003ccode\u003e{\"__type__\": \"Tensor\", \"shape\": [1, 768]}\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis means you can route gigabyte-sized biological tensors across \u003ccode\u003eAbstractManifold\u003c/code\u003e nodes while retaining cryptographic, EU AI Act-compliant audit traces for every step.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eEU AI Act Compliance\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-eu-ai-act-compliance\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: EU AI Act Compliance\" href=\"#eu-ai-act-compliance\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eLár-JEPA is architecturally structured to satisfy the requirements of the European Union AI Act for high-risk systems. dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eAbstractCognitiveNode\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e — Universal base class. Any model type implements this to become routable. Declares its \u003ccode\u003eModelType\u003c/code\u003e and exposes \u003ccode\u003eencode()\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eforward()\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003edecode()\u003c/code\u003e contract. The spine never inspects beyond this interface. An LLM, a JEPA world model, a GNN, and a diffusion model are all identical from the executor's perspective.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eAbstractManifold\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e — JEPA-specific subclass of \u003ccode\u003eAbstractCognitiveNode\u003c/code\u003e for continuous latent-space world models. Specialises the interface to \u003ccode\u003eembed_context()\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003epredict_target()\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003eentropic_loss()\u003c/code\u003e. Any architecture implementing this is routable in a \u003ccode\u003eBatchNode\u003c/code\u003e alongside \u003ccode\u003eLLMNode\u003c/code\u003e instances without modification.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eAbstractContextBridge\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e — Stateless signal adapters for cross-modal composition. Allows LLMs to attend to JEPA latent predictions and JEPAs to condition on LLM semantic embeddings — without either node knowing about the other's internals.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eAbstractLatentFaultLocator\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e — Formal specification of the Topological Vulnerability Targeting Engine (\u003ccode\u003ecore/interfaces.py\u003c/code\u003e). cross-attention (environmental state as Query, structural sequence as Key/Value), and extract the top-k structural positions at highest risk.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content Any future implementation extending this ABC and passing invariants I1–I6 is a Derivative Work of this specification (Apache 2.0, prior art anchored by RFC 3161 certificate and Zenodo DOIs \u003ccode\u003e10.5281/zenodo.19245328\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e10.5281/zenodo.19484646\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e10.5281/zenodo.19646405\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eRun the full invariant suite:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"pytest lar_jepa/tests/unit/test_latent_fault_locator_invariants.py -v\n# 32 passed: materials_domain · seismic_domain · network_infrastructure_domain · industrial_domain\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003epytest lar_jepa/tests/unit/test_latent_fault_locator_invariants.py -v\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e 32 passed: materials_domain · seismic_domain · network_infrastructure_domain · industrial_domain\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eAbstractAttentionKernel\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e — Decouples the attention \u003cem\u003emechanism\u003c/em\u003e from the fault localisation pipeline. Any mechanism producing a normalised distribution over N positions and extracting k ordered indices satisfies the specification. Six invariants (A1–A6). Reference implementations: \u003ccode\u003eScaledDotProductKernel\u003c/code\u003e (softmax(QKᵀ/√D)), \u003ccode\u003eCosineAttentionKernel\u003c/code\u003e. Valid future implementations: \u003ccode\u003eLinearAttentionKernel\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eSparseAttentionKernel\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eSSMKernel\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eHyenaKernel\u003c/code\u003e — any mechanism satisfying A1–A6 is a Derivative Work.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eAbstractPerturbationOperator\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e — Formal specification of latent-space counterfactual prediction. Formalises the pattern:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"Δ      = encode_mutant(x_mut) − encode_wildtype(x_wt)\nz_pred = z_ctrl + α · Δ\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eΔ      = encode_mutant(x_mut) − encode_wildtype(x_wt)\nz_pred = z_ctrl + α · Δ\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eZero-shot intervention prediction in any domain — without executing the intervention in the physical world. Six invariants (P1–P6). Reference implementations: \u003ccode\u003eCrystalDefectOperator\u003c/code\u003e (perfect vs defect-injected crystal), \u003ccode\u003eMolecularBindingOperator\u003c/code\u003e (unbound vs ligand-bound conformation), \u003ccode\u003eBearingDegradationOperator\u003c/code\u003e (healthy vs degraded sensor signature), \u003ccode\u003eInterestRateShockOperator\u003c/code\u003e (baseline vs stressed portfolio), \u003ccode\u003eLateralMovementOperator\u003c/code\u003e (current-hop vs next-hop network state), \u003ccode\u003eCO2ShockOperator\u003c/code\u003e (baseline vs elevated-forcing atmosphere), \u003ccode\u003eSensorDegradationOperator\u003c/code\u003e (nominal vs adverse-weather perception). Domain instantiations: materials defect simulation, molecular dynamics, industrial condition monitoring, quantitative finance, network security, climate modelling, autonomous vehicle perception.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eAbstractRoutingKernel\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e — Decouples routing \u003cem\u003elogic\u003c/em\u003e from routing \u003cem\u003emechanism\u003c/em\u003e. Formalises the score-then-route pattern enabling deterministic, learned, probabilistic, and adaptive routing on the same graph executor. Four invariants (R1–R4). Reference implementations: \u003ccode\u003eEntropicThresholdKernel\u003c/code\u003e (current Lár-JEPA pattern), \u003ccode\u003eMultiThresholdRoutingKernel\u003c/code\u003e. Valid future implementations: \u003ccode\u003eLearnedPolicyKernel\u003c/code\u003e (RL), \u003ccode\u003eEnsembleVoteKernel\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eUncertaintyKernel\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eCalibratedBayesianKernel\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eAbstractModalEncoder\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e — Universal modality-to-latent-space encoding interface. Separates domain-specific encoding logic from all downstream attention, routing, and memory operations — enabling plug-and-play encoder replacement without modifying any other pipeline component. Three invariants (M1–M3). Reference implementations: \u003ccode\u003eElectrochemicalEncoder\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eNetworkTelemetryEncoder\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eMarketStateEncoder\u003c/code\u003e (price/vol/macro), \u003ccode\u003eVibrothermalEncoder\u003c/code\u003e (vibration/temperature), \u003ccode\u003eAtmosphericStateEncoder\u003c/code\u003e (ERA5 reanalysis), \u003ccode\u003eCameraEncoder\u003c/code\u003e (BEV patch features), \u003ccode\u003eLidarEncoder\u003c/code\u003e (range-view point cloud). Valid future implementations: spectroscopic encoder, protein structure encoder, seismic sensor encoder — any architecture producing \u003ccode\u003e(B, output_dim)\u003c/code\u003e output satisfies M1–M3.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eAbstractDivergenceRouter\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e \u003cem\u003e(tenth ABC — v2.3.0)\u003c/em\u003e — Multi-stream routing primitive. Keeps two independent latent streams separate, measures their geometric divergence, and treats high-confidence disagreement as the primary control signal rather than noise to be averaged away. Seven invariants (V1–V7). The Investigate rule is the key contribution: when both streams are confident but contradictory, the divergence is flagged as \u003ccode\u003eTRIGGER_REPLAN\u003c/code\u003e — not fused, not averaged. When used as training infrastructure, high-divergence cases automatically accumulate as \u003ccode\u003eD_hard\u003c/code\u003e — the self-curating curriculum at the model's uncertainty boundary. The \u003cstrong\u003eSafety-Learning Equivalence\u003c/strong\u003e (V6, proved in \u003ca href=\"https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20278781\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eDOI 10.5281/zenodo.20278781\u003c/a\u003e) establishes that the invariants enforcing routing safety are identical to the invariants making divergence a valid training signal. \u003cstrong\u003eDifficulty Invariance\u003c/strong\u003e (V7, proved in \u003ca href=\"https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20614051\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eDOI 10.5281/zenodo.20614051\u003c/a\u003e) establishes that the D_hard curriculum is world-grounded: failure-class geometry persists across encoder upgrades — difficulty is a property of the input, not the encoder version. Domain instantiations: medical imaging (scan vs. report), vision-language (image vs. caption), autonomous vehicles (sensor vs. map), cybersecurity (behaviour vs. policy).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eRun the full interface invariant suite (151 tests total):\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"pytest lar_jepa/tests/unit/ -v\n# 151 passed across AbstractLatentFaultLocator (I1–I6), AbstractAttentionKernel (A1–A6),\n# AbstractPerturbationOperator (P1–P6), AbstractRoutingKernel (R1–R4), AbstractModalEncoder (M1–M3)\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003epytest lar_jepa/tests/unit/ -v\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e 151 passed across AbstractLatentFaultLocator (I1–I6), AbstractAttentionKernel (A1–A6),\u003c/span\u003e\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e AbstractPerturbationOperator (P1–P6), AbstractRoutingKernel (R1–R4), AbstractModalEncoder (M1–M3)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eJEPA_DMN_Consolidation_Node\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e — Live bridge writing committed JEPA trajectories into any \u003ccode\u003eAbstractDMN\u003c/code\u003e implementation (from \u003ccode\u003elar-dmn\u003c/code\u003e). Ingests committed trajectories as Tier 1 episodic events via \u003ccode\u003edmn.ingest()\u003c/code\u003e; retrieves prior heuristics via \u003ccode\u003edmn.recall()\u003c/code\u003e. Accepts any \u003ccode\u003eAbstractDMN\u003c/code\u003e subclass — or uses a local in-memory fallback for demos.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eCrystalJEPA\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e — A real JEPA model for battery materials. Three-component architecture: \u003ccode\u003eCrystalSiteEncoder\u003c/code\u003e (2-layer Transformer over 20 elemental sites), EMA \u003ccode\u003eTargetEncoder\u003c/code\u003e (no gradients), and a \u003ccode\u003ePredictor\u003c/code\u003e that maps visible-site context to masked-site representations. Trained with JEPA loss — MSE in latent space with stop-gradient on the target. 68,736 parameters. Trains to 97% loss reduction in 61 seconds on CPU. <p dir="auto"><strong>The universal routing nervous system for heterogeneous cognitive architectures.</strong></p>
<p align="center" dir="auto">
  <a href="https://github.com/snath-ai/lar">
    <img alt="Spine" src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/c3247be25a72f982accc9196c69a51fdad602bfc0fe2509fda77fa620f891eae/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f5370696e652d4cc3a172253230456e67696e6525323076322e322e322d626c75653f7374796c653d666f722d7468652d6261646765" data-canonical-src="https://img.shields.io/badge/Spine-Lár%20Engine%20v2.2.2-blue?style=for-the-badge" style="max-width: 100%;">

<hr>
<p dir="auto">Every agentic framework built so far assumes one model type. LangChain assumes LLMs. When a JEPA world model outputs a 768-dimensional latent tensor, those frameworks crash — there is no signal type for it.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Lár-JEPA routes anything.</strong> LLMs, JEPAs, diffusion models, SSMs, GNNs — as first-class nodes in the same deterministic graph. The execution spine does not inspect model internals. It routes <code>AbstractCognitiveNode</code> instances. What the node does internally is irrelevant.</p>
<p dir="auto">This is the difference between a framework built for chatbots and an architecture built for the next decade of AI research.</p>
<hr>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The Problem</h2><a id="user-content-the-problem" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The Problem" href="#the-problem"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">LLM agents hallucinate because their "memory" is a linear string of text. When step 3 of a 50-step plan goes wrong, the entire execution is doomed — the model has no internal model of physics, spatial logic, or long-term consequence. It predicts the next token.</p>
<p dir="auto">JEPA world models solve this by predicting future states in latent space — planning by simulating consequences mathematically before any action touches the real world. But JEPAs don't output text. They output tensors. No existing framework can route them.</p>
<hr>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">What Lár-JEPA Enables</h2><a id="user-content-what-lár-jepa-enables" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: What Lár-JEPA Enables" href="#what-lár-jepa-enables"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="# LLM → JEPA: LLM decides, JEPA simulates

# Monte Carlo search in latent space
BatchNode([JEPANode(action="ACCELERATE"), JEPANode(action="BRAKE"), JEPANode(action="TURN")])
→ ReduceNode(output_key="best_action")

# Heterogeneous swarm — any mix

# Any future architecture

    model_type = ModelType.FUTURE
    # Routes without modification"><pre><span class="pl-c"># LLM → JEPA: LLM decides, JEPA simulates</span>
<span class="pl-en">LLMNode</span>(<span class="pl-s1">output_key</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"action_spec"</span>) → <span class="pl-v">JEPANode</span>(<span class="pl-s1">output_key</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"predicted_state"</span>)

<span class="pl-c"># JEPA → LLM: JEPA predicts, LLM reasons over the prediction</span>
<span class="pl-en">JEPANode</span>(<span class="pl-s1">output_key</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"latent_prediction"</span>) → <span class="pl-v">LLMNode</span>(<span class="pl-s1">prompt_template</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"Given state {latent_prediction}..."</span>)

<span class="pl-c"># Monte Carlo search in latent space</span>
<span class="pl-en">BatchNode</span>([<span class="pl-en">JEPANode</span>(<span class="pl-s1">action</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"ACCELERATE"</span>), <span class="pl-en">JEPANode</span>(<span class="pl-s1">action</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"BRAKE"</span>), <span class="pl-en">JEPANode</span>(<span class="pl-s1">action</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"TURN"</span>)])
→ <span class="pl-en">ReduceNode</span>(<span class="pl-s1">output_key</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"best_action"</span>)

<span class="pl-c"># Heterogeneous swarm — any mix</span>
<span class="pl-en">BatchNode</span>([<span class="pl-en">LLMNode</span>(...), <span class="pl-en">JEPANode</span>(...), <span class="pl-en">GNNNode</span>(...)])

<span class="pl-c"># Any future architecture</span>
<span class="pl-k">class</span> <span class="pl-v">MyFutureNode</span>(<span class="pl-v">AbstractCognitiveNode</span>):
    <span class="pl-s1">model_type</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-v">ModelType</span>.<span class="pl-c1">FUTURE</span>
    <span class="pl-c"># Routes without modification</span></pre></div>

<p dir="auto"><code>AbstractCognitiveNode</code> is the only contract the Lár executor requires
